subtasks.title: Initialize Next.js frontend with TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, and DaisyUI
subtasks.description: Set up the frontend project with Next.js, TypeScript, styling libraries, and internationalization support
subtasks.details:
1. Create a new Next.js project with TypeScript support using `npx create-next-app@latest --typescript` 2. Install and configure Tailwind CSS following the official documentation 3. Add DaisyUI as a Tailwind plugin by installing it with `npm install daisyui` 4. Configure DaisyUI in the tailwind.config.js file 5. Set up next-i18next for internationalization: - Install with `npm install next-i18next` - Create locales folder with en and ar translation files - Configure next-i18next.config.js - Modify _app.tsx to use the appWithTranslation HOC 6. Create a basic folder structure following modular architecture: - components/ (shared UI components) - features/ (feature-specific components) - pages/ (Next.js pages) - styles/ (global styles) - utils/ (utility functions) - hooks/ (custom React hooks) - types/ (TypeScript type definitions) 7. Test the setup by creating a simple page with internationalized content and DaisyUI components ## Implementation Plan 1. Create a new Next.js project with TypeScript support: - Run `npx create-next-app@latest --typescript my-project` - Navigate to project directory: `cd my-project` - Initialize Git repository if not already done: `git init` 2. Install and configure Tailwind CSS: - Install required packages: `npm install -D tailwindcss postcss autoprefixer` - Generate configuration files: `npx tailwindcss init -p` - Update tailwind.config.js with content paths: ```js module.exports = { content: [ "./pages/**/*.{js,ts,jsx,tsx}", "./components/**/*.{js,ts,jsx,tsx}", "./features/**/*.{js,ts,jsx,tsx}" ], theme: { extend: {}, }, plugins: [], } ``` - Add Tailwind directives to globals.css: ```css @tailwind base; @tailwind components; @tailwind utilities; ``` 3. Add DaisyUI as a Tailwind plugin: - Install DaisyUI: `npm install daisyui` - Update tailwind.config.js to include DaisyUI: ```js module.exports = { // ... existing config plugins: [require("daisyui")], daisyui: { themes: ["light", "dark"], }, } ``` 4. Set up next-i18next for internationalization: - Install required packages: `npm install next-i18next react-i18next i18next` - Create locales folder structure: ``` /public /locales /en common.json /ar common.json ``` - Add sample translations to common.json files - Create next-i18next.config.js in root: ```js module.exports = { i18n: { defaultLocale: 'en', locales: ['en', 'ar'], localeDetection: true, }, } ``` - Update next.config.js to use i18n config: ```js const { i18n } = require('./next-i18next.config') module.exports = { i18n, reactStrictMode: true, } ``` - Modify _app.tsx to use appWithTranslation: ```tsx import { appWithTranslation } from 'next-i18next' import type { AppProps } from 'next/app' import '../styles/globals.css' function MyApp({ Component, pageProps }: AppProps) { return } export default appWithTranslation(MyApp) ``` 5. Create modular folder structure: - components/ (shared UI components) - ui/ (basic UI elements) - layout/ (layout components) - features/ (feature-specific components) - pages/ (Next.js pages) - styles/ (global styles) - utils/ (utility functions) - hooks/ (custom React hooks) - types/ (TypeScript type definitions) - lib/ (third-party library configurations) 6. Create sample components to test the setup: - Create a Button component in components/ui/ - Create a Layout component in components/layout/ - Update index.tsx to use i18n and DaisyUI components: ```tsx import { useTranslation } from 'next-i18next' import { serverSideTranslations } from 'next-i18next/serverSideTranslations' export default function Home() { const { t } = useTranslation('common') return (

{t('welcome')}

) } export async function getStaticProps({ locale }) { return { props: { ...(await serverSideTranslations(locale, ['common'])), }, } } ``` 7. Test the complete setup: - Run the development server: `npm run dev` - Verify that: - Tailwind CSS styles are applied - DaisyUI components render correctly - Internationalization works when switching languages - TypeScript type checking works properly

subtasks.title: Set up NestJS backend with TypeScript and PostgreSQL
subtasks.description: Initialize the backend project with NestJS, configure PostgreSQL connection, and implement API documentation
subtasks.details:
1. Create a new NestJS project using `nest new backend --package-manager npm`
2. Configure TypeScript settings in tsconfig.json for strict type checking
3. Install and set up PostgreSQL dependencies:
   - Install TypeORM and PostgreSQL driver: `npm install @nestjs/typeorm typeorm pg`
   - Create a database configuration module
   - Configure database connection in app.module.ts
4. Set up environment variables management with @nestjs/config
5. Implement a modular folder structure:
   - modules/ (feature modules)
   - common/ (shared utilities, guards, filters)
   - config/ (configuration files)
   - interfaces/ (TypeScript interfaces)
   - entities/ (TypeORM entities)
6. Configure Swagger for API documentation:
   - Install Swagger packages: `npm install @nestjs/swagger swagger-ui-express`
   - Set up Swagger in main.ts
   - Create a basic health check endpoint and document it with Swagger decorators
7. Test the database connection and API documentation by running the application

subtasks.title: Configure Docker and CI/CD pipeline
subtasks.description: Set up Docker for development environment and implement a basic CI/CD pipeline
subtasks.details:
1. Create Dockerfiles for both frontend and backend:
   - Frontend Dockerfile with Node.js and Next.js configuration
   - Backend Dockerfile with Node.js and NestJS configuration
2. Create a docker-compose.yml file that includes:
   - Frontend service
   - Backend service
   - PostgreSQL database service
   - Volume configurations for persistent data
   - Environment variables configuration
3. Configure networking between services
4. Set up development-specific Docker configurations:
   - Hot reloading for both frontend and backend
   - Debug configurations
5. Create .dockerignore files for both projects
6. Implement a basic CI/CD pipeline using GitHub Actions or similar:
   - Create workflow YAML files for CI/CD
   - Configure linting and testing steps
   - Set up build process for Docker images
   - Configure deployment steps (can be placeholder for now)
7. Document the Docker setup and CI/CD process in README.md
8. Test the complete setup by building and running the application with Docker Compose

tasks.title: Task #11: Fix i18n Key Duplication in Frontend Components
tasks.description: Investigate and resolve the issue where internationalization (i18n) keys and their translated text are both appearing simultaneously on pages, particularly in components with asynchronous translation loading.
tasks.details:
This task requires a systematic approach to debugging the i18n implementation:

1. Identify affected components:
   - Create an inventory of all components displaying the duplication issue
   - Document the specific patterns of duplication (e.g., key format, affected languages)
   - Determine if the issue is limited to specific routes or global

2. Code investigation:
   - Review the i18n initialization process and configuration
   - Examine how translation keys are registered and loaded
   - Check for race conditions in asynchronous translation loading
   - Investigate component lifecycle methods that might trigger premature rendering
   - Look for missing fallback mechanisms when translations aren't yet available

3. Potential solutions:
   - Implement proper loading states for translations
   - Add conditional rendering to prevent displaying raw keys
   - Ensure translation hooks/components properly handle async loading
   - Consider implementing a global translation loading state
   - Review and refactor the i18n provider implementation if necessary

4. Implementation:
   - Create a fix that addresses the root cause rather than symptoms
   - Ensure backward compatibility with existing components
   - Document any API changes or new patterns for the team
   - Update relevant documentation on i18n usage

5. Performance considerations:
   - Measure and minimize any impact on initial page load time
   - Consider implementing translation caching if not already present
   - Evaluate bundle size impact of any new i18n libraries or code
tasks.testStrategy:
Testing should be comprehensive to ensure the issue is fully resolved:

1. Manual testing:
   - Create a test matrix covering all supported languages
   - Test on all affected pages and components
   - Verify proper rendering during page load, navigation, and dynamic content updates
   - Test with network throttling to simulate slow translation loading
   - Verify behavior when switching languages dynamically

2. Automated testing:
   - Create or update unit tests for the i18n utility functions
   - Implement component tests that verify proper rendering with async translations
   - Add integration tests that simulate the full translation loading process
   - Create snapshot tests to catch unexpected rendering changes

3. Regression testing:
   - Verify that all previously working i18n features still function correctly
   - Check that no new duplicate keys appear in other components
   - Ensure performance metrics remain within acceptable thresholds

4. Edge case testing:
   - Test with missing translations
   - Test with very long translated strings
   - Test with RTL languages if supported
   - Test with browser language preferences set to various options

5. Documentation validation:
   - Verify that any updated i18n usage patterns are clearly documented
   - Create examples for the team showing proper implementation
